newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire negotiation team delays trip to South Africa.
newsitem.headline: Zaire negotiation team delays trip to South Africa.

text.p: The team due to represent Zaire's central authorities in talks with rebels said on Wednesday it was delaying its departure for the venue in South Africa by a day to coordinate strategy.

A member of the seven-man committee appointed by embattled President Mobutu Sese Seko said the team would meet on Thursday to harmonise their views on the agenda of the talks and leave for Pretoria on Friday.
"We have to get together tomorrow. It's important to know what the agenda will be in South Africa," Ngoy Nduba, a Mobutu supporter, told Reuters.

The team, headed by Mobutu's security adviser Honore Ngbanda, includes representatives from the opposition and Mobutu supporters. Their departure was originally set for Thursday for the talks at the weekend.
The delegation reflects widely divergent positions of the opposition and presidency. A senior government official said Ngbanda was expected to have the final word on crucial issues.
The rebels, who took up arms in October and who vow to topple Mobutu, have said that the talks would lead to a meeting between their leader, Laurent Kabila, and Mobutu.
Rebel spokesmen have said that Mobutu, who seized power in 1965, has to negotiate his departure.
It was not immediately clear if the travel schedule of the negotiators had been affected by Tuesday night's nomination of a new prime minister by Zaire's opposition alliance.
The alliance nominated Mobutu's arch-foe and radical firebrand Etienne Tshisekedi, who has long favoured negotiations with Kabila. Mobutu was expected to endorse the nomination.
